ask_text: --issue 140: an unbalanced quote defeats the blanket-staging gate in 59 bytes with no timeout, and the test suite documents the bypass as correct behaviour.

events.note: architectural (mandatory trigger: security domain + hook/gate keywords). 8 reqs/8 ACs, falsifiability clean. Root cause independently verified by orchestrator: the redirection arm at pre-tool-use.sh:1153 marks the heredoc delimiter as a redirect target but never treats the body as an opaque region, so quote-state leaks through. q1 (which shell the Bash tool actually invokes) non-blocking, recorded.

Phase 2 round 1: DBA APPROVE_WITH_NOTES (major: AC1 has no fixture cell for <<- tab-stripped terminators, a genuinely different mechanism than quote parity - independently verified by orchestrator against real bash). DevOps APPROVE_WITH_NOTES (resolved q1: production shell is zsh, confirmed by inspecting its own subprocess; also independently rediscovered the main-branch corpus-drift issue). SecOps REQUEST_CHANGES: core vulnerability confirmed live via two independent oracles with real non-zero controls (26-byte repro, shim-confirmed git invocation), but R1's fixture matrix only crosses one implicit delimiter spelling - SecOps proved <<-EOF and <<'EOF' are ALSO live-exploitable with the identical odd-quote body and are outside AC1's binding matrix, so an implementation could pass every AC while shipping 2 of 3 proven-exploitable spellings. Looping back to BA per the rubric.

Round 2: AC1 widened to 12 cells crossing delimiter-introducer spelling as its own axis; AC9/AC10/AC11 added. 11 ACs, falsifiability clean, contiguous. Orchestrator independently reproduced the <<-EOF composition claim in real bash.

Round 2 closed clean: DBA APPROVE, DevOps and SecOps APPROVE_WITH_NOTES, 0 blocking. SecOps re-verified against literal cell definitions (not the summary), independently caught <<\EOF was untested and verified it live, found AC10 omits a low-risk <<\EOF narrow-stage cell. DevOps independently re-confirmed main is still red on the corpus-drift issue across 3 consecutive runs.

Judge synthesized sketch A (smallest blast radius) as winner, grafting 3 items from sketch B; owner_decision.required=false (sketches converged on mechanism, differed only on reviewability/blast-radius, a technical call). Judge's own empirical check surfaced a genuine, live regression neither Phase-2 round tested: full heredoc-body opacity for an UNQUOTED introducer flips a construction the CURRENT scanner correctly denies today (unquoted <<EOF body containing $(git add -A), via an accidental '(' -driven mechanism) into an allow post-fix, and real zsh/bin-sh genuinely execute that substitution -- a direct violation of spec's own R1 ('mirror a real shell's own treatment') for the unquoted case. Orchestrator routed this to SecOps for a real ruling rather than deciding solo, per the standing instruction to leverage the pipeline for high-risk items. SecOps independently re-reproduced against the actual gate driver AND real zsh/bin-sh (own non-zero control caught first: a non-numeric issue-dir silently produced 'none' for everything including a sanity control), confirmed the finding exactly, ruled it is NOT comparable to the already-accepted #118 verb-opacity gap (this is a fix-introduced regression in the same control the fix is meant to harden, not a pre-existing unrelated gap), and VETOed: closing 4 proven bypasses while opening a comparably-easy 5th in the same commit is not proportionate to ship silently. Specified the minimum spec fix: a narrow additive AC (not a redesign) -- for an UNQUOTED heredoc introducer only, deny outright if the body contains a literal $(, backtick, or ${ before the real terminator; quoted-delimiter bodies stay fully opaque exactly as already specified (confirmed correct against real zsh). SecOps also independently found and reported, as an OUT-OF-SCOPE separate finding, a more severe, currently-untracked, pre-existing bypass: bare backtick substitution (`git add -A`) defeats the gate today with no heredoc at all, because backtick is not in the scanner's structural-character set -- filed as new issue #143, not blocking #140. Full evidence at .pipeline/140/secops-2.5-ruling.json. Looping back to BA for a narrow AC12 addition per SecOps's spec, NOT a full redesign; sketches/design.json stand and are not re-run once the spec is widened, per the standard VETO loop-back.

Round 3 (VETO rework): added AC12 verbatim per SecOps's required_minimum_spec_change -- for an unquoted heredoc introducer, deny outright if the body contains a literal $(, backtick, or ${ before the real terminator; quoted-delimiter bodies stay fully opaque per AC1/R1, unchanged. 4 fixture cells added, all taken verbatim from SecOps's own real-gate-driver-plus-real-zsh reproduction. 12 ACs total, falsifiability-clean, contiguous. R1-R8/AC1-AC11 confirmed byte-identical, q1 not reopened, design.json/sketches untouched (additive-only, no redesign needed).

Round 3 closed clean, scoped confirmation only (not a full re-review of AC1-AC11, already approved twice). DBA APPROVE: confirmed AC12 touches no schema/migration/access-policy surface. DevOps APPROVE: confirmed AC12 is in-process only, no subprocess/network/CI/deploy surface. SecOps VETO LIFTED, APPROVE_WITH_NOTES: AC12 checked field-by-field against SecOps's own required_minimum_spec_change (scope condition, three literal sequences, coarse fail-closed minimum, non-weakening of quoted-delimiter opacity, all 4 fixture cells) -- faithful match, no drift or scope narrowing. One non-blocking note: ${ has no dedicated real-shell repro cell (unlike $( and backtick), a fail-closed defense-in-depth choice under R1 rather than a proven-exploit cell -- recommended as a nice-to-have 5th regression cell for QA, not a gate. Phase 2.5 does not re-run (design.json/sketches stand, additive-only per BA's and the judge's own synthesis); proceeding directly to Phase 3.
